name: Jihadist spillover into coastal West Africa (Benin, Togo)
started: 2025-10-28 (JNIM's first claimed attack in Nigeria; attacks in northern Benin and Togo date back to 2021-22)
summary: JNIM is pushing south from Burkina Faso's eastern forests into northern Benin and Togo and, since October 2025, into western Nigeria. Benin had its deadliest year on record in 2025 with 305 militant-linked deaths (Africa Center) and lost 15 soldiers in a single raid in March 2026. It matters because these are relatively stable coastal states with ports that feed the whole Sahel.

sides.name: Coastal state security forces
members: Togolese Armed Forces (Operation Koundjoare, Savanes region)
Nigerian Armed Forces in Kwara and Niger states (Operation Savanna Shield from Feb 2026)
backers: No major external military deployment documented in sources found
sides.strength: Benin: 3,000-troop northern force since 2022 plus 5,000 more recruits for the north (Africanews, Mar 2026).

sides.name: JNIM
members: JNIM units based in Burkina Faso's Est region and the W-Arly-Pendjari forests
JNIM emir for Benin (appointed per UN reporting)
leaders: Unnamed senior eastern leader tasked with expansion into Benin, Cote d'Ivoire, Ghana, Niger and Togo (UN report via AFP)

background: The W, Arly and Pendjari parks, a forest complex shared by Benin, Burkina Faso and Niger, give JNIM cover from air strikes and income from poaching, timber and artisanal gold. From there it has staged into Benin's Alibori and Atacora departments and Togo's Savanes region since 2021-22. Benin's worst single loss came in April 2025, when JNIM killed 54 soldiers in W National Park.

UN reporting says JNIM appointed a senior eastern commander for expansion into Benin, Cote d'Ivoire, Ghana, Niger and Togo, and an emir for Benin. Why it matters: the coastal states' northern borderlands have long-standing grievances (herder-farmer tensions, park evictions) that JNIM exploits, and the corridor reaches toward Nigeria's Kainji Lake area, where several jihadist groups now overlap.
year: JNIM claimed its first attack inside Nigeria on 28 Oct 2025 at Nuku, Kwara state, killing one soldier and seizing weapons (ACLED). Benin survived a coup attempt against President Talon on 7 Dec 2025. JNIM's regional offensive from early February 2026 reached Benin with ambushes on patrols and attacks on police and customs posts, a Chinese-run construction site and a school, then large raids on army positions at Kofouno (Alibori) and the former Pendjari Lodge (Atacora) on 4 and 7 March; the army said 15 soldiers died at Kofouno, JNIM claimed 11 across both, and JNIM seized an M113 armoured personnel carrier. In late May JNIM attacked positions in Koualou, a disputed border enclave with Burkina Faso, killing several soldiers and civilians. Benin held elections in January (parliament, where the ruling bloc won all 109 seats) and April (presidency, won by Romuald Wadagni). In Togo, the Africa Center counted at least 54 civilians and 8 soldiers killed in the year to early 2026.
situation: As of late October 2026, JNIM is entrenched in the parks along Benin's northern border and active in Togo's Savanes and the Benin-Nigeria-Niger borderlands. Benin's new president inherits a northern front with repeated base raids. No peace process exists. The Kainji/Borgu zone in Nigeria, where JNIM, Boko Haram cells, Lakurawa and Mahmuda all operate, is the next frontier (see the Nigeria northwest entry).
technical: JNIM uses the W-Arly-Pendjari forest complex as a sanctuary; forests provide cover from air strikes plus income from illegal timber and gold (Defense Post/AFP).

4 and 7 Mar 2026 raids on Kofouno and the former Pendjari Lodge destroyed infrastructure and seized weapons and an M113 APC; Benin said its aircraft killed at least four attackers as they withdrew, and 21 militants in total (ACLED; Africanews).
Early-2026 JNIM campaign in Benin also hit soft targets: police and customs posts, a Chinese-run construction site and a school (ACLED).
Benin's force posture: a 3,000-troop northern force created in 2022 plus 5,000 additional recruits for the north (Africanews).
Togo's northern operation is called Operation Koundjoare (Benin Web TV).
JNIM's Benin push followed the defection to ISSP of Sadou Samahouna, a senior JNIM Est commander and brother of JNIM's Niger emir (ACLED).
First claimed JNIM attack in Nigeria: Nuku, Kwara state, 28 Oct 2025, one soldier killed, weapons and equipment seized (ACLED).
Koualou, a disputed Benin-Burkina border enclave, was attacked in May 2026 with weapons and materiel seized (ACLED).
casualties: Africa Center (2025 data): Benin 305 militant-linked fatalities, up 76% and its deadliest year on record; Togo at least 54 civilians and 8 soldiers killed over the past year. 2026 incidents: Kofouno, 15 soldiers killed and 5 wounded (Benin army, March 2026). No rolling 12-month total found.
displaced: No figures found in sources retrieved for northern Benin or Togo.

timeline.event: Background: JNIM kills 54 Beninese soldiers in W National Park.
JNIM claims first attack in Nigeria, at Nuku, Kwara state.
Failed coup attempt against Benin's President Talon.
JNIM raids Kofouno army position in Alibori; 15 soldiers killed.
JNIM raids the former Pendjari Lodge position in Atacora.
Romuald Wadagni wins Benin's presidential election.
JNIM attack on military positions in Koualou reported.

outlook: Watch the dry season for further base raids in Alibori and Atacora, any JNIM attacks further south or in Togo's Savanes, cooperation (or not) between Benin and the Sahel juntas, and whether JNIM consolidates in Nigeria's Kainji-Borgu belt.

zones.name: W-Arly-Pendjari forest complex
zones.note: JNIM sanctuary straddling Benin, Burkina Faso and Niger; site of the April 2025 attack that killed 54 Beninese soldiers and of the March 2026 Pendjari Lodge raid.

zones.name: Togo Savanes region (Dapaong)
zones.note: JNIM infiltration from Burkina Faso; Operation Koundjoare area.

zones.name: Koualou enclave
zones.note: Disputed Benin-Burkina border area; JNIM attack May 2026 (location approximate).

battles.name: JNIM raids on Kofouno and Pendjari Lodge positions
battles.place: Kofouno, Alibori, and former Pendjari Lodge, Atacora, Benin (mapped at Kofouno, approximate)
battles.outcome: Bases pillaged and burned; attackers withdrew under air attack.
battles.forces: JNIM assault groups; Benin garrisons with air support.
battles.losses: Benin army: 15 soldiers killed and 5 wounded at Kofouno; 21 militants killed in total. JNIM claimed 11 soldiers killed across both. An M113 APC seized.
battles.significance: Benin's deadliest raid of 2026, during its election season, showing JNIM's ability to hit fixed positions along the Niger border.
